chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated.
That Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was asked, while I was listening, about shade for the muḥrim in the case of harm from rain or sun—or, he said, from an illness.
So he commanded the expiation of a sheep, which he should slaughter in Minā.
And he said: “When we wish to do that, we seek shade and offer the expiation.”

key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Minā, the location of the sacrifice
key_terms.فِدَاءِ: expiatory compensation required for the act
key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: for the person in the state of iḥrām

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a muḥrim taking shade due to rain, sun, or illness?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling for the muḥrim who needs shade because of harm from rain, sun, or illness. In such a case, taking shade is allowed with fidyah, specifically the sacrifice of a sheep in Minā. The Imam عليه السلام also states that this was their own practice when needed.
